newsitem.title: GERMANY: German consumer inflation averaged 1.5 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: German consumer inflation averaged 1.5 pct in 1996.

text.p: German consumer price inflation averaged 1.5 percent in 1996, slowing from 1.8 percent the year before, the Federal Statistics Office said on Wednesday.
In west Germany, 1996 inflation was 1.4 percent, down from 1.7 percent the year before, while in east Germany it was 2.2 percent, up slightly from 2.1 percent, the office said.
In December, final inflation data for all Germany showed consumer prices rose 0.3 percent from the previous month and 1.4 percent from a year earlier.
Prices in west Germany were also up 0.3 percent and 1.4 percent, respectively, while in east Germany they rose 0.1 percent from the previous month and 1.6 percent from the year-earlier month.
Seasonal foods showed a strong 1.9 percent month-on-month price rise in December, mainly due to an 11 percent rise in prices for fresh vegetables, the office said.
Fruit prices, however, fell 1.6 percent, and potatoes declined 2.4 percent.
Energy prices, minus fuel, rose 0.4 percent, mainly due to a 1.7 percent rise in heating oil. Heating oil prices were up 23.7 percent from the year before.
